key_insight: This paper examines whether a permissionless, blockchain-based trust layer for AI agents can actually make unknown agents more trustworthy in practice. It studies ERC-8004—the first decentralized trust protocol for AI agents—by empirically analyzing how its Identity, Reputation, and Validation registries work in the real world.
problem_solved: Autonomous AI agents increasingly need to transact with unfamiliar counterparts across organizational boundaries, but there is no standard way to assess trust in a decentralized setting. The paper addresses the gap between the promise of trustless agent economies and the lack of empirical evidence about whether ERC-8004’s trust signals are reliable and useful.
method: Empirical study of the ERC-8004 decentralized AI agent ecosystem.
Analysis of the protocol’s three on-chain registries: Identity, Reputation, and Validation.
Evaluation of whether on-chain trust information is informative enough for agents to judge unknown peers.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners building agentic systems, this work helps clarify whether decentralized trust infrastructure can support safe autonomous coordination. It provides evidence to guide adoption of blockchain-based reputation and validation mechanisms in multi-agent and cross-organization deployments.
visual_elements: Three-registry diagram showing Identity → Reputation → Validation
Trust flow chart illustrating how an agent evaluates an unknown counterpart
Blockchain/network icon set representing decentralized agent interactions
Simple bar or matrix chart comparing the usefulness of different trust signals
paper_title: Can Trustless Agents Be Trusted? An Empirical Study of the ERC-8004 Decentralized AI Agent Ecosystem
paper_authors: Xihan Xiong, Zelin Li, Wei Wei, Qin Wang, William Knottenbelt
